60	Experiments reveal that unconditional correction is universally harmful: CRM applied at every step degrades all four LIBERO suites (up to $-$14.8\,pp; Section~\ref{sec:failure_modes}). The 80--97\% of steps where the VLA is already confident receive corrections that are noise. The solution is a calibrated gating mechanism that detects confident steps and suppresses correction accordingly.
61	
62	\paragraph{Why $K{=}2$.}
63	\looseness=-1 $K{=}2$ is the minimum sample size that admits a pairwise disagreement measure, and under batched inference the uncertainty signal is \emph{free}: $K{=}2$ latency (${\sim}$170\,ms) matches $K{=}1$ because both samples share the same prefix encoding and flow-matching denoising runs in parallel (Table~\ref{tab:efficiency}). Empirically, the $K{=}2$ $L_2$ distance ranks steps in nearly identical order to $K{=}10$ sample variance ($\rho{=}0.9979$; Table~\ref{tab:proxy_comparison}), establishing ordering consistency of the proxy; this measures relative uncertainty ranking, not predictive validity for action correctness. Step-level validity is established indirectly through the suite-level monotonic correlation between trigger rate and performance recovery (Figure~\ref{fig:trigger_scatter}). Three alternative probes, including CRM correction magnitude ($K{=}1$ and $K{=}2$) and flow-matching velocity dispersion (FMVD), all fail ($\rho < 0.16$). Under the K-matched comparison ($K{=}2$ for both), calibrated $\tau$-gating exceeds unconditional correction on all four evaluated suites ($\Delta_{\mathrm{gate}}{=}{+}2.8$ to $+$14.5\,pp; Section~\ref{sec:main_results}).

1	We show that learned post-hoc correction of frozen flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models is harmful by default, not because the correction module is poor, but because the vast majority of control steps do not need it. On most steps, the VLA already produces confident, low-variance actions; corrections applied here act as noise, degrading performance across all evaluated task suites and model scales. This motivates a shift from improving correction quality to deciding \emph{when to correct at all}. We propose a calibrated gating mechanism that draws two stochastic action samples from the frozen VLA in a single batched forward pass, at zero extra latency, and uses their pairwise distance as a per-step uncertainty proxy. A threshold on this distance gates a lightweight correction module: confident steps pass through unchanged, while only genuinely uncertain steps receive learned residual correction. Across four LIBERO manipulation suites on two VLAs spanning an order of magnitude in scale, selective gating recovers nearly all degradation caused by unconditional correction, with recovery magnitude correlating monotonically with task difficulty. The key finding is that knowing when \emph{not} to correct matters more than the correction itself.

1	\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related_work}
2	
3	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{VLA robustness.} VLAs have progressed from tokenized prediction~\cite{brohan2023rt2,kim2024openvla,ghosh2024octo} to flow matching~\cite{black2024pi0,shukor2025smolvla}, yet lose over 65\,pp under deployment perturbations~\cite{fei2025liberoplus}. Training-time defenses~\cite{srpo2025,robustvla2025,digflow2025,liu2026ttvla} improve robustness but require retraining.
4	
5	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{Inference-time correction.} Among frozen-VLA methods, ReconVLA~\cite{chen2026reconvla} quantifies uncertainty without learned correction; SC-VLA~\cite{liu2026scvla} requires RL; VLA-Pilot~\cite{li2025vlapilot} uses evolutionary search at 2.41\,s per step. A2C2~\cite{a2c2_2025}, the closest concurrent work, learns a correction head for temporal staleness but applies it unconditionally. Our pipeline detects \emph{when correction would hurt}, using calibrated gating to suppress correction on confident steps. Residual policy learning~\cite{silver2018residual,johannink2019residual} shares the additive structure; magnitude control is addressed by gating~\cite{jiang2024transic}, clipping~\cite{xiao2026pld}, or decay~\cite{pan2025drc}. Our CRM uses fixed $L_2$ clipping with supervised loss, requiring no RL.
6	
7	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{Selective prediction.} Our $\tau$-gating is an instance of selective prediction~\cite{chow1970optimum,elyaniv2010selective,geifman2017selective}. Unlike SelectiveNet~\cite{geifman2019selectivenet}, we use a pairwise distance threshold with no additional learned components. The $K{=}2$ $L_2$ distance is a minimal ensemble disagreement measure~\cite{lakshminarayanan2017simple}, requiring no architectural changes. Conformal prediction~\cite{angelopoulos2023gentle} has been applied to robotics~\cite{lindemann2023safe,luo2024conformalized,chen2025cpnav}; our threshold draws on this calibration philosophy without formal coverage guarantees.

Our finding is established for the tested lightweight MLP-based CRM; whether larger correction architectures or online fine-tuning would change this conclusion remains open. The method requires stochastic action diversity from the base VLA; deterministic models produce vacuous multi-sample signals (Appendix~\ref{sec:applicability}), establishing an architectural boundary. The CRM is trained on $K{=}10$ argmin-selected actions but deployed at $K{=}2$, creating a distribution shift that may limit correction quality; matched-$K$ training is a natural extension. The threshold $\tau$ is suite-dependent (Appendix~\ref{sec:tau_sweep}), recovery on $\pi_{0.5}$ is partial (Appendix, Table~\ref{tab:tau_sweep_pi05}), and all experiments use the LIBERO simulation benchmark; whether the degradation--recovery pattern transfers to other simulation environments, real-robot deployment with visual domain shift, or task domains beyond tabletop manipulation remains untested.

"""
Magnitude sensitivity curve — half-column stacked layout for combined figure.
Top: LIBERO-Object (multi-seed), Bottom: LIBERO-Spatial (seed 42).
Output: magnitude_curve.pdf
"""

import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import ScalarFormatter

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['Times New Roman'],
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 7,
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'lines.linewidth': 1.5,
    'lines.markersize': 5,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.03,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
})

# === LIBERO-Object data (Director-locked, 2026-05-18) ===
obs_only_object = {
    0.03: [16],
    0.05: [13, 15, 15, 14],
    0.10: [19, 16, 17, 16, 15, 14],
    0.20: [22, 16, 16, 16, 15, 20, 18],
    0.30: [19, 18, 14, 17, 16],
    1.42: [17, 16, 10],
}

perdof_object = {
    0.03: [14],
    0.05: [14, 9],
    0.10: [11, 11, 8, 13, 12, 11],
    0.20: [11, 9, 10, 12, 9, 11, 7],
    0.30: [4, 5, 5],
    1.42: [0, 0, 0],
}

vla_only_obj_seeds = [12, 12, 10, 11, 13]
argmin_obj_seeds = [12, 17, 13, 12, 10, 10]
vla_only_obj_mean = np.mean(vla_only_obj_seeds)
argmin_obj_mean = np.mean(argmin_obj_seeds)

# === LIBERO-Spatial data (seed 42 only) ===
eps_spatial = np.array([0.05, 0.10, 0.30, 1.42])
obs_only_spatial = np.array([35, 35, 36, 35])
perdof_spatial = np.array([31, 35, 26, 0])
argmin_spatial = 34
vla_only_spatial = 30

# === Plotting: 2-row × 1-col stacked layout ===
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(3.3, 3.8), sharex=False)

# --- Top: LIBERO-Object with multi-seed error bars ---
eps_vals = sorted(obs_only_object.keys())
obs_means = [np.mean(obs_only_object[e]) for e in eps_vals]
obs_stds = [np.std(obs_only_object[e], ddof=1) if len(obs_only_object[e]) > 1 else 0 for e in eps_vals]
obs_ns = [len(obs_only_object[e]) for e in eps_vals]

per_eps = sorted(perdof_object.keys())
per_means = [np.mean(perdof_object[e]) for e in per_eps]
per_stds = [np.std(perdof_object[e], ddof=1) if len(perdof_object[e]) > 1 else 0 for e in per_eps]
per_ns = [len(perdof_object[e]) for e in per_eps]

eps_arr = np.array(eps_vals)
per_arr = np.array(per_eps)

ax1.axvspan(0.05, 0.2, alpha=0.06, color='#6FA8D2', zorder=0)

ax1.plot(eps_arr, obs_means, '-', color='#6FA8D2', linewidth=1.5, zorder=4)
obs_multi_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(obs_ns) if n > 1]
obs_single_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(obs_ns) if n == 1]
if obs_multi_idx:
    ax1.errorbar(eps_arr[obs_multi_idx], [obs_means[i] for i in obs_multi_idx],
                 yerr=[obs_stds[i] for i in obs_multi_idx], fmt='o', color='#6FA8D2',
                 markerfacecolor='#6FA8D2', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
                 capsize=3, capthick=0.8, elinewidth=0.8, label='obs\_only', zorder=5)
if obs_single_idx:
    ax1.plot(eps_arr[obs_single_idx], [obs_means[i] for i in obs_single_idx], 'D',
             color='#6FA8D2', markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='#6FA8D2',
             markeredgewidth=1.0, markersize=5, zorder=5)

ax1.plot(per_arr, per_means, '--', color='#D08888', linewidth=1.5, zorder=4)
per_multi_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(per_ns) if n > 1]
per_single_idx = [i for i, n in enumerate(per_ns) if n == 1]
if per_multi_idx:
    ax1.errorbar(per_arr[per_multi_idx], [per_means[i] for i in per_multi_idx],
                 yerr=[per_stds[i] for i in per_multi_idx], fmt='^', color='#D08888',
                 markerfacecolor='#D08888', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
                 capsize=3, capthick=0.8, elinewidth=0.8, label='perdof', zorder=5)
if per_single_idx:
    ax1.plot(per_arr[per_single_idx], [per_means[i] for i in per_single_idx], 'D',
             color='#D08888', markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='#D08888',
             markeredgewidth=1.0, markersize=5, zorder=5)

ax1.axhline(argmin_obj_mean, color='#555555', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.9,
            label=f'Argmin ({argmin_obj_mean:.1f}%)', zorder=2)
ax1.axhline(vla_only_obj_mean, color='#999999', linestyle='-.', linewidth=0.7,
            label=f'VLA-only ({vla_only_obj_mean:.1f}%)', zorder=2)

ax1.set_xscale('log')
ax1.set_xticks(eps_arr)
ax1.xaxis.set_major_formatter(ScalarFormatter())
ax1.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(plt.NullFormatter())
ax1.set_xticklabels(['0.03', '0.05', '0.1', '0.2', '0.3', r'$\sim$1.42'])
ax1.set_xlabel(r'$\varepsilon$')
ax1.set_ylabel('SR (%)')
ax1.set_ylim(-2, 28)
ax1.set_xlim(0.025, 2.0)
ax1.set_title('LIBERO-Object', fontsize=10, pad=3)
ax1.legend(loc='upper left', framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='none',
           borderpad=0.3, handlelength=1.5)
ax1.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='-', alpha=0.15, zorder=0)
ax1.set_axisbelow(True)

# --- Bottom: LIBERO-Spatial (seed 42) ---
ax2.axvspan(0.05, 0.2, alpha=0.06, color='#6FA8D2', zorder=0)

ax2.plot(eps_spatial, obs_only_spatial, 'o-', color='#6FA8D2',
         markerfacecolor='#6FA8D2', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
         label='obs\_only', zorder=5)
ax2.plot(eps_spatial, perdof_spatial, '^--', color='#D08888',
         markerfacecolor='#D08888', markeredgecolor='white', markeredgewidth=0.5,
         label='perdof', zorder=5)

ax2.axhline(argmin_spatial, color='#555555', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.9,
            label=f'Argmin ({argmin_spatial}%)', zorder=2)
ax2.axhline(vla_only_spatial, color='#999999', linestyle='-.', linewidth=0.7,
            label=f'VLA-only ({vla_only_spatial}%)', zorder=2)

ax2.annotate('0%', xy=(1.42, 0), xytext=(0.8, 6),
             fontsize=7, color='#D08888', fontweight='bold', ha='center',
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#D08888', lw=0.7))

ax2.set_xscale('log')
ax2.set_xticks(eps_spatial)
ax2.xaxis.set_major_formatter(ScalarFormatter())
ax2.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(plt.NullFormatter())
ax2.set_xticklabels(['0.05', '0.1', '0.3', r'$\sim$1.42'])
ax2.set_xlabel(r'$\varepsilon$')
ax2.set_ylabel('SR (%)')
ax2.set_ylim(-3, 42)
ax2.set_xlim(0.04, 2.0)
ax2.set_title('LIBERO-Spatial (seed 42)', fontsize=10, pad=3)
ax2.legend(loc='lower left', framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='none',
           borderpad=0.3, handlelength=1.5)
ax2.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle='-', alpha=0.15, zorder=0)
ax2.set_axisbelow(True)

plt.tight_layout(h_pad=1.2)

out_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
fig.savefig(os.path.join(out_dir, 'magnitude_curve.pdf'), format='pdf')
fig.savefig(os.path.join(out_dir, 'magnitude_curve.png'), format='png', dpi=300)
plt.close()

print("Saved: magnitude_curve.pdf, magnitude_curve.png")
